scenes.headline: How an agent loop wrote contest-winning GPU kernels
scenes.sub: auto-gpu-kernel: one change per turn, checked before it is timed.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Parsnip! Auto GPU Kernel is a Claude Code loop that won a kernel contest track with nobody watching. Here's the loop.

scenes.label: The loop
scenes.text: Change one thing at a time, check correctness before timing anything, and write every result, failures too, to files that outlive the context.
scenes.say: It changes one thing at a time, checks correctness before timing anything, and writes every result, even failures, to files.

steps.say: Each turn reads three files on disk, a rulebook, a summary and a lessons log, then plans exactly one change.

steps.note: a failing kernel gets no latency at all
steps.say: It implements the change and validates it first. A wrong kernel never gets timed at all.
Only then is it measured, and logged, even a loss. Ninety-eight experiments, thirty-two kept.
The biggest win came after a workload inspector was added: a sub-agent that reads the inputs, not the code.

scenes.title: The biggest win does no arithmetic

left.title: Top-k by scoring
items: Score every token in the FP8 cache
left.say: The indexer's job is to pick the two thousand and forty-eight highest-scoring tokens.

right.title: The scoreless fast path
items: At 2048 tokens or fewer, every valid token wins
right.say: But when a sequence is shorter than that, every valid token is the answer, so the kernel just expands the page table.

items.say: A batch of at most eight tokens can't fill the chip, so each token is split sixteen ways.
Valid slots come first, so each split takes every sixteenth slot, not one chunk.

items.text: Split and combine in one launch
items.say: Then split and combine share one launch, behind an atomic barrier.

scenes.label: the arithmetic mean of per-workload ratios against a reference wrapper
scenes.note: that wrapper copies the whole 624 MB paged KV cache every call
scenes.say: The headline, thirty-four point nine three times, averages ratios against a wrapper that copies the whole cache every call.

scenes.text: The loop's edge is bookkeeping: one change, correctness before speed, and every failure written down.

recap: Plan, implement, validate, measure, log, repeat
Correctness is checked before anything is timed
Look at the inputs, not just the code
scenes.say: To recap: one change per turn, correctness before timing, and an inspector that reads the inputs.
